title: ASAS-3 eclipse times of 2000-2009 support the 592-day third body of HD 303514 and limit its mass to 1.2-5 solar masses; joint fits predict the shallowest eclipses in 2030-2035, not eclipse loss
abstract: HD 303514 is a detached 19.897-day eclipsing binary whose eclipses became shallower from 2002 to 2026. SCI work found a third body in TESS eclipse times (2019-2026; outer period 584-600 d) but could not limit its mass from above. We used the archival ASAS-3 V photometry of 2000-2009 as independent timing data. A sinusoidal timing term at the TESS outer period improves the ASAS-3 light-curve likelihood by 14-18 (-2 delta lnL; semi-amplitude 30-36 min). Night-block bootstrap simulations give a false-alarm probability of 0.005 inside the TESS period window, but 0.058 for a blind search from 150 to 3,000 d. We measured 11 ASAS-3 eclipse times (errors 7-26 min). The 17 published three-body solutions do not predict them (chi-square 55-4,000). A joint Newtonian three-body fit of 18 TESS times, 8 TESS impact parameters, 6 ASAS-3 depths and the 11 ASAS-3 times gives chi-square 46.9 for 30 degrees of freedom: third-body mass m3 = 2.0 solar masses for an inner-pair mass of 4, outer period 591.7 d, e2 = 0.25, mutual inclination 5 deg. The mass profile gives m3 = 1.2-3.1 solar masses (delta chi-square < 4). Two other groupings of the ASAS-3 eclipses move the best mass to 1.9 and 3.1 and the upper limit to about 5. Heavy dark third bodies of 7-12 solar masses are rejected (delta chi-square >= 35). One main-sequence A-type third star of about 2 solar masses agrees with the light. In the accepted solutions the primary impact parameter reaches 1.89-1.94 stellar radii in 2029.8-2033.1 and the secondary 1.94-1.97 in 2031.3-2034.7, below the loss limit of 2. The eclipses then deepen again. At the minimum the secondary depth is 11-42 percent of its 2026 value. We give eclipse-time predictions for TESS sectors 111-113 (December 2026 to February 2027). Limits: sparse ASAS-3 photometry, chunk times that depend on an eclipse template, a mild joint tension (p = 0.026), local fits without a posterior, and a twin-star eclipse model whose systematic errors are comparable to the margin to eclipse loss.

citations.reason: TESS eclipse times, impact parameters, three-body model code and 17 solutions used here. ASAS-3 timing supports its 592-day third body and its no-loss forecast, but rejects its heavy-mass solutions and moves the shallowest-eclipse epoch later.
